actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.

dimensions.assessment: Affects members of the public seeking postal services in communities where post offices experience temporary emergency suspensions.
dimensions.evidence: The Postal Service shall develop and maintain a publicly available website with an interactive web-tool that provides information about each covered post office

dimensions.assessment: Provides administrative transparency and data access regarding suspended post office locations, reasons, alternative services, and reopening estimates.
dimensions.evidence: a street address; the date on which the relevant emergency suspension... took effect; the reason for such emergency suspension; alternative services available

dimensions.assessment: Involves administrative costs for the Postal Service to develop and maintain a website and database, but no major federal spending or revenue changes are stated.
Amends title 39 of the United States Code to mandate a specific online transparency tool and bulk data download functionality.
dimensions.evidence: Subchapter VII of chapter 36 of title 39, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following new section

dimensions.assessment: Establishes a permanent ongoing requirement for the Postal Service to maintain the website, with a one-year implementation deadline.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Postal Service shall establish the website

missing_information: Estimated cost to the Postal Service of building and maintaining the website.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill requires the U.S. Postal Service to build and maintain a public website providing searchable, downloadable information on post offices experiencing emergency suspensions.
